## Tutorials

TheStringclass has a set of built-in methods that you can use on strings.

Java Strings Tutorial

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThecharAt()method returns the character at the specified index in a string.

The index of the first character is 0, the second character is 1, and so on.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return the first character (0) of a string:
String myStr = "Hello";
char result = myStr.charAt(0);
System.out.println(result);
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThecodePointAt()method returns the Unicode 
value of the character at the specified index in a string.

The index of the first character is 0, the second character is 1, and so on.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return the Unicode of the first character in a string (the Unicode value 
  of "H" is 72):
String myStr = "Hello";
int result = myStr.codePointAt(0);
System.out.println(result);
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThecodePointBefore()method returns the Unicode 
value of the character before the specified index in a string.

The index of the first character is 1, the second character is 2, and so on.

Note:The value 0 will generate an error, as this is a negative number (out 
of reach).

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return the Unicode of the first character in a string (the Unicode value 
  of "H" is 72):
String myStr = "Hello";
int result = myStr.codePointBefore(1);
System.out.println(result);
Try it Yourself »
```

## Tutorials

❮ String Methods

ThecodePointCount()method returns the 
number of Unicode values found in a string.

Use thestartIndexandendIndexparameters to specify where 
to begin and end the search.

The index of the first character is 0, the second character is 1, and so on.

### Code Examples

```
Example
Return the number of Unicode values found in a string:
String myStr = "Hello";
int result = myStr.codePointCount(0, 5);
System.out.println(result);
Try it Yourself »
```
